organizer_statements.quote: Pixels corresponding to known USGS/INGENIOUS faults are masked / excluded from evaluation, so they do not count towards penalty terms. ... Re-evaluation will also mask/exclude the existing USGS/INGENIOUS faults. ... for scoring purposes it should not matter whether these known faults are included with predictions or not.
organizer_statements.consequence_used_here: This is the exact statement that makes a dot on a known fault FREE BUT WORTHLESS: it is removed from the penalty terms and, under the only reading that makes the staff's closing sentence literally true, also from the credit term. gems44.metric implements that reading and tests it (tests/test_metric.py::test_known_mask_is_neutral).

organizer_statements.what_it_establishes: Participants asked which data the NLR/USGS experts used, whether the new faults are surface or buried, and whether coverage was uniform. A DrivenData staff reply exists in the thread; the thread page render returned the participant posts and did not expose the staff reply text to the fetch tool. Therefore this repo does NOT claim to know the provenance of the hidden faults.
organizer_statements.irregularity: IR-44-01: the organizers' answer to the provenance question could not be read by the fetch tool from this sandbox. Any downstream claim about the hidden fault population must remain a labelled model, not a fact.

organizer_statements.what_it_would_establish: Cited by GEMSDOE32 as containing a clarification that a new fault may be new geometry of an existing system. This repo did NOT verify that thread and therefore makes NO claim based on it. H1, which would have relied on that idea, was falsified empirically instead.

provenance_caveat: The four files above are owner-supplied mirrors of login-walled DrivenData competition files, pinned by sha256. Pins prove REPRODUCIBILITY, not organizer authentication. The irregularity is registered as IR-44-02.

sandbox_reachability_test.consequence: This sandbox CAN fetch raw files from the owner's public GitHub repositories through the GitHub contents API (verified by hash), and CANNOT fetch data from USGS, GDR/OpenEI, or any GitHub Pages site. Every external-data claim in registry/hypotheses.json is graded against this measured list.
